title: Признание Луи в кладовой  (Louis's Confession in the Storage Room)

segments.t: In the storage room, the persistent female guest corners Louis and says she missed him terribly. Louis awkwardly confesses that she was the very first girl he ever slept with and that they cannot be together, only for Chef Barinov to burst in reciting poetry.
Луи, извини, что я отвлекаю тебя от работы.
Просто я очень соскучился.
Я так и знала.
Нет, нет, нет.
Ты вообще единственная девушка, с которой я...
Слава богу.
Поэтому между нами ничего не может быть.
Я что, такая страшная?
Ты делал это как настоящий мужчина.
Мальчик мой?
Ну-ка, живы на кухню.
Мне очень скучно, нужно бежать.
Это он?
Let's replay the exchange and look closely at each Russian phrase.
Луи, извини, что я отвлекаю тебя от работы.
'Louis, forgive me for distracting you from your work.' Nastya anchors the line on 'Louis', while 'of work' completes the thought.
Просто я очень соскучился.
'I just missed you so much.' In Russian, the idea of 'just' flows naturally into 'to miss' without extra filler words. Nastya answers right away.
Я так и знала.
'I knew it all along.' The grammar packs 'I' and 'knew' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
Нет, нет, нет.
'No, no, no.' The grammar packs 'there is no' and 'there is no' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
Ты вообще единственная девушка, с которой я...
'You are actually the only girl I have ever...' Notice how Russian expresses 'you' and 'I' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Louis answers right away.
Слава богу.
'Thank goodness for that.' Louis brings out the contrast between 'glory' and 'to God' in a few short words.
Поэтому между нами ничего не может быть.
'That is why nothing can ever happen between us.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'therefore' before landing on 'maybe'.
Я что, такая страшная?
'What, am I really that ugly?' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'I' and finishing on 'terrible'. Nastya answers right away.
Ты делал это как настоящий мужчина.
'You did it like a real man.' Nastya addresses the listener with the informal singular 'you' alongside 'man'.
Мальчик мой?
'My little boy?' Louis anchors the line on 'boy', while 'my' completes the thought.
Ну-ка, живы на кухню.
'Alright, get back to the kitchen alive.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'go on' before landing on 'kitchen'. Louis answers right away.
Мне очень скучно, нужно бежать.
'I am terribly sorry, I have to run.' The grammar packs 'for me' and 'to run' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
Это он?
'Wait, is that him?' Nastya brings out the contrast between 'this' and 'he' in a few short words. Let's hear the complete conversation once more.

That wraps up this scene as louis tries to tell his female admirer in the storage room that nothing can happen between them after their one night together, just as Chef Barinov barges in reciting poetry. See you next time!
